claims.text: CoFeNiV is a magnetic high-entropy alloy.

A first-principles plus machine-learning model integrating spin-polarized electronic-structure descriptors and lattice-distortion parameters will improve phonon thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy by approximately 30% over conventional models.
The combined descriptors capture additional phonon-scattering channels.
The additional phonon-scattering channels are mediated by local electronic-density fluctuations and spin-induced lattice distortions.
Local electronic-density fluctuations and spin-polarized lattice distortions modulate phonon lifetimes and scattering rates.
Correlating spin-resolved density of states with concurrent lattice distortions can reveal previously unaccounted phonon-scattering channels.
The proposed additional scattering channels reduce phonon lifetimes.
Calibration against experimental measurements will make the spin-polarized descriptors accurately capture the proposed effects.
Arc melting followed by annealing can produce CoFeNiV with a uniform phase distribution.
The proposed approach is primarily applicable to high-entropy alloys with significant magnetic contributions.
The approach is limited to regimes in which spin-resolved electronic properties and their effects on phonon scattering can be reliably measured.
The magnitude of the proposed accuracy improvement depends on successful calibration of the spin-polarized descriptors.
Variability in the experimental extraction of spin-polarized descriptors may cause deviations from the predicted performance.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines improvement as reduced model prediction error relative to conventional models, whereas the falsification rule asks whether experimentally determined lifetimes and conductivity themselves show an improvement over conventional predictions. Measured physical values do not improve; prediction errors do. This makes the benchmark internally inconsistent.

One statement treats significant deviation of measurements from the integrated model's forecasts as decisive, while the other requires failure to achieve approximately 30% improvement or failure of a descriptor-scattering correlation. These are not equivalent falsification criteria.
